To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the unfolding process of the N-terminal domain of creatine kinase is slowed down by subunit interaction in high urea concentrations.
the N-terminal domain of the muscle type creatine kinases (CKs) is protected from unfolding by the interaction between subunits.
the subunit interactions of muscle type creatin kinase are important in protecting the N-terminal domain from urea unfolding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of subunit interaction on the unfolding process of CK-MM.
the subunit protection of CK-MM in urea unfolding and the role of subunit interaction in CK-MM folding.
the role of subunit interactions in the unfolding of CK and provides a novel method for studying the subunit interactions of proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
subunit interactions are important in the stabilization of the CK-MM molecule in urea.
subunit interaction slows the unfolding rate constants and preserves secondary structure and contracted conformation at the N-terminal domain in CK-MM.
subunit interactions are very important in preserving the structure of the N-terminal domain of muscle type creatin kinase in urea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-terminal domain is more resistant to unfolding than the C-terminal domains, and that the subunit interactions play an important role in the unfolding of CK.
subunit interaction plays a role in the stability and folding of CK.
subunit interactions play important roles in stabilizing the CK-MM dimer in urea and that subunit interaction in urea can be used to distinguish the CK-MM domain from the CK-BB domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
subunit interaction plays a key role in protecting the N-terminal domain of the dimer from unfolding during the denaturation process of CK in urea.
the unfolding of CK is not a single step process but a complex process that involves the unfolding of each domain in a different manner.
the N-terminal domain of muscle type CK is well protected by subunits and the protection is lost at high urea concentration.
